events.title: Mary, Queen of Scots, Is Born
events.description: Mary Stuart was born at Linlithgow Palace in Scotland. Her father, James V, died just days later, so she became queen when she was only six days old.
events.significance: Her turbulent reign, her claim to the English throne and her execution in 1587 shaped the politics of Britain. Her son James later united the crowns of Scotland and England.

events.title: Mathematician George Boole Dies
events.description: The English mathematician and logician George Boole died in Ballintemple, County Cork, Ireland. He was a self-taught scholar who became the first professor of mathematics at Queen's College, Cork.
events.significance: His system of algebraic logic, now called Boolean algebra, became the foundation of digital circuits and computer programming.

events.title: Second Vatican Council Closes
events.description: Pope Paul VI formally closed the Second Vatican Council in Rome. The gathering of the world's Catholic bishops had met over four years.
events.significance: The council reshaped modern Catholicism. It allowed Mass in local languages, encouraged dialogue with other faiths and redefined the role of lay people in the Church.

events.title: John Lennon Is Murdered in New York
events.description: Former Beatle John Lennon was shot outside the Dakota apartment building in Manhattan as he returned home from a recording session. He was 40.
events.significance: His death shocked the world and ended any hope of a Beatles reunion. It prompted a global outpouring of grief and renewed debate over gun violence.
